subproblems.title: Mollification of a Lipschitz function: smooth, same gradient bound, uniformly close, local (Simon's f^(σ))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, g : ℝ^P → ℝ K-Lipschitz and σ > 0. Then there is a C^∞ function g' : ℝ^P → ℝ such that ‖Dg'(x)‖ ≤ K for every x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ g' x), |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ for every x, and g'(x) = c whenever x ∈ ℝ^P and c ∈ ℝ are such that g(y) = c for every y in the open ball B_σ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (K : NNReal) (σ : ℝ), LipschitzWith K g → 0 < σ → ∃ g' : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g' ∧ (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ g' x‖ ≤ K) ∧ (∀ x, |g' x - g x| ≤ K * σ) ∧ ∀ (x : Euclid P) (c : ℝ), (∀ y ∈ ball x σ, g y = c) → g' x = c

It is reused here with a byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new worker is provisioned. The argument below is that node's accepted proof, written out self-contained.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.8–4.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 1401–1402: for a Lipschitz f use the mollification f^(σ) = f ∗ φ_σ), and step 1 of the parent proof (mollified cut-offs). Let λ := volume, Lebesgue measure on ℝ^P = Euclid P. It is translation invariant, invariant under x ↦ −x, and finite on compact sets.

1. (Normalized mollifier.) There is ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ that is C^∞, has compact support, satisfies ψ ≥ 0 and ∫ψ dλ = 1, and has support ψ ⊆ B_σ(0). Indeed, take a C^∞ bump function φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] centred at 0 with φ = 1 on B_{σ/2}(0) and support φ = B_σ(0); such bump functions exist on every finite-dimensional inner product space. φ is continuous with compact support and positive on the nonempty open ball B_σ(0), so 0 < ∫φ dλ < ∞, and ψ := φ/∫φ dλ has all the properties. (The accepted Lean proof takes ψ from the accepted declaration Submission.dgcr_stc_exists_normalized_mollifier with r := σ.)
2. (Definition.) Put g'(x) := ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y), the convolution ψ ⋆ g. For each x the integrand is continuous with compact support (inside the closed ball of radius σ), hence integrable.
3. (Smoothness.) g is K-Lipschitz, hence continuous and locally integrable, and ψ is C^∞ with compact support. So g' is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left, after writing g' as the convolution of ψ and g with ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ).
4. (Gradient bound.) For x, x' ∈ ℝ^P, g'(x) − g'(x') = ∫ ψ(y)·(g(x − y) − g(x' − y)) dλ(y), and |g(x − y) − g(x' − y)| ≤ K‖x − x'‖. Since ψ ≥ 0 and ∫ψ dλ = 1, |g'(x) − g'(x')| ≤ K‖x − x'‖. So g' is K-Lipschitz (in the accepted Lean proof this is Submission.cmcs_ls_mollify_lipschitz). As g' is differentiable, ‖Dg'(x)‖ ≤ K for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
5. (Uniform approximation.) Fix x. Since ∫ψ dλ = 1, g'(x) − g(x) = ∫ ψ(y)·(g(x − y) − g(x)) dλ(y). For y ∈ support ψ ⊆ B_σ(0), |g(x − y) − g(x)| ≤ K‖y‖ ≤ K·σ, and the integrand vanishes elsewhere. With ψ ≥ 0 this gives |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ·∫ψ dλ = K·σ (Mathlib's dist_convolution_le).
6. (Locality.) Suppose g(y) = c for every y ∈ B_σ(x). For y ∈ support ψ ⊆ B_σ(0) we have x − y ∈ B_σ(x), so g(x − y) = c. Hence g'(x) = c·∫ψ dλ = c. ∎
proof_key_steps: Normalized mollifier ψ: C^∞, compact support, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ψ = 1, support ψ ⊆ B_σ(0).
g' := ψ ⋆ g is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
g' is K-Lipschitz (ψ ≥ 0, ∫ψ = 1), so ‖Dg'‖ ≤ K (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
|g' − g| ≤ Kσ because |g(x − y) − g(x)| ≤ Kσ on support ψ; g'(x) = c when g ≡ c on B_σ(x).

Then there exist functions h_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and a real constant c such that: every h_k is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (h_k)); ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ c for all k and x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ (h_k) x); |h_k(x)| ≤ 2 for all k and x; and h_k → h uniformly on ℝ^P as k → ∞ (TendstoUniformly along atTop).

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (mollified cut-offs h_k of h = γ_{a,b}∘f), with the mollification supplied by the sibling lipschitz_smoothing (Lean Submission.cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing: for a K-Lipschitz g : ℝ^P → ℝ and σ > 0 there is a C^∞ function g' with ‖Dg'(x)‖ ≤ K and |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ for every x). Instead of the parent's scales δ_k = 1/(k+1) we use σ_k = 1/((K+1)(k+1)), which also gives the uniform bound |h_k| ≤ 2.

Notation: δ := b − a > 0; γ(s) := min{1, max{0, (b − s)/δ}} for s ∈ ℝ; h := γ∘f, i.e. h(x) = min{1, max{0, (b − f(x))/δ}}; K := (1/δ)·L ≥ 0 (in Lean the NNReal `Real.toNNReal (b - a)⁻¹ * L`, whose coercion to ℝ is (b − a)⁻¹·L).

1. (γ is (1/δ)-Lipschitz.) For all reals u, v: |min{1, u} − min{1, v}| ≤ |u − v| and |max{0, u} − max{0, v}| ≤ |u − v| (min or max with a constant is 1-Lipschitz; Lean: `abs_min_sub_min_le_max` followed by `simp`, and `abs_max_sub_max_le_abs` after rewriting `max 0 u = max u 0` with `max_comm`). For s, t ∈ ℝ put u := (b − s)/δ and v := (b − t)/δ; then |u − v| = |s − t|/δ. Hence |γ(s) − γ(t)| ≤ (1/δ)·|s − t| (`LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul`).
2. (h is K-Lipschitz.) For x, y ∈ ℝ^P, |h(x) − h(y)| ≤ (1/δ)·|f(x) − f(y)| ≤ (1/δ)·L·‖x − y‖ = K·‖x − y‖ (`LipschitzWith.comp` of step 1 with the hypothesis `LipschitzWith L f`).
3. (|h| ≤ 1.) max{0, u} ≥ 0 and min{1, ·} ≤ 1, so 0 = min{1, 0} ≤ h(x) ≤ 1 and |h(x)| ≤ 1 for every x.
4. (Scales.) For k ∈ ℕ let σ_k := 1/((K + 1)(k + 1)) > 0. Since 0 ≤ K ≤ K + 1, K·σ_k = K/((K + 1)(k + 1)) ≤ 1/(k + 1) ≤ 1.
5. (Smoothing.) For each k apply the sibling lipschitz_smoothing to g := h (K-Lipschitz by step 2), the constant K and σ := σ_k > 0. Choosing one witness for each k (Lean: `choose`) gives functions h_k : ℝ^P → ℝ such that h_k is C^∞ (`ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (h_k)`), ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ K for every x, and |h_k(x) − h(x)| ≤ K·σ_k ≤ 1/(k + 1) for every x (step 4). The locality clause of the sibling is not used.
6. (Conclusion.) Take these h_k and c := K. Smoothness of every h_k and ‖Dh_k(x)‖ ≤ c for all k, x are step 5. For every k and x, |h_k(x)| ≤ |h_k(x) − h(x)| + |h(x)| ≤ 1/(k + 1) + 1 ≤ 2 (steps 3–5). Uniform convergence: given ε > 0 choose N ∈ ℕ with 1/(N + 1) < ε (`exists_nat_one_div_lt`); for every k ≥ N and every x, dist(h(x), h_k(x)) = |h_k(x) − h(x)| ≤ 1/(k + 1) ≤ 1/(N + 1) < ε. By `Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff` this is `TendstoUniformly (fun k => h_k) h atTop`, with h written as `fun x => min 1 (max 0 ((b - f x) / (b - a)))`. ∎

subproblems.title: Simon's identity 4.11 via integral representations: T(g dη) − ∂T(gη) = −T(dg∧η)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (k+1)) and let μ, μ' be measures on ℝ^P. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) take values in the continuous linear functionals on covectors (MultiVector). Assume:
- T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U);
- ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for all θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and η ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then, as real numbers (Bochner integrals, with no integrability assumed),
∫ g(x)·ξ(x)(dη(x)) dμ(x) − ∫ g(x)·ξ'(x)(η(x)) dμ'(x) = −∫ ξ(x)(alternatizeUncurryFin((Dg(x)).smulRight(η(x)))) dμ(x),
where dη = exteriorDerivative η and Dg(x) = fderiv ℝ g x. Informally: T(g dη) − ∂T(gη) = −T(dg∧η).

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386): T(γ∘f dω) − T(d(γ∘f ω)) = −T(γ'(f) df∧ω). Here an arbitrary C^∞ function g replaces γ∘f, and T and ∂T are written through their integral representations. This is step 2 (Leibniz identity (i)) of the parent proof. No integrability is used: every equality of integrals below is either a representation hypothesis or integral_congr_ae applied to a pointwise identity, and the latter holds for arbitrary functions.

Notation: η̂ := (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k), dη̂ := exteriorDerivative η̂, Dg(x) := fderiv ℝ g x, and D(x) := alternatizeUncurryFin((Dg(x)).smulRight(η̂(x))). Write hT and hbT for the representation hypotheses of T and of T.boundary, and hg for the smoothness of g.

1. (Multiplying test forms by g.) Let m ∈ ℕ and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U). The form gω : x ↦ g(x)•ω(x) is C^∞, as a product of C^∞ maps (ContDiff.smul). It vanishes wherever ω vanishes, so tsupport(gω) ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_smul_subset_right). Now tsupport ω is compact and contained in U, and tsupport(gω) is a closed subset of it, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). So gω ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
2. (Test forms used.)
   - dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U); its underlying form is dη̂.
   - η_g := gη̂ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and ω_g := g dη̂ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U), by step 1.
   - dη_g := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η_g; its underlying form is exteriorDerivative(gη̂).
   - D_T := dη_g − ω_g ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U), a difference in the submodule; its underlying form is the pointwise difference.
3. (Leibniz rule.) Fix x. Since g and η̂ are C^∞, both are differentiable at x (ContDiff.differentiable, with 1 ≤ ∞). By definition exteriorDerivative θ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ θ x) (extDeriv). The product rule (fderiv_fun_smul) gives fderiv ℝ (gη̂) x = g(x)•fderiv ℝ η̂ x + (Dg(x)).smulRight(η̂(x)). Since alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and ℝ-homogeneous (alternatizeUncurryFin_add, alternatizeUncurryFin_smul), exteriorDerivative(gη̂)(x) = g(x)•dη̂(x) + D(x). Hence the underlying form of D_T at x is exteriorDerivative(gη̂)(x) − g(x)•dη̂(x) = D(x) (abel).
4. (First integral.) Each ξ(x) is linear, so ξ(x)(g(x)•dη̂(x)) = g(x)·ξ(x)(dη̂(x)) (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). By integral_congr_ae and hT at ω_g, ∫ g ξ(dη̂) dμ = ∫ ξ(x)(ω_g(x)) dμ = T(ω_g).
5. (Second integral.) Likewise ξ'(x)(g(x)•η̂(x)) = g(x)·ξ'(x)(η̂(x)). We use integral_congr_ae, hbT at η_g, and ∂T(θ) = T(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k θ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, which holds by rfl). This gives ∫ g ξ'(η̂) dμ' = ∂T(η_g) = T(dη_g).
6. (Linearity of T.) T acts through the ℝ-linear map T.toCurrent. So T(ω_g) − T(dη_g) = −T(dη_g − ω_g) = −T(D_T) (LinearMap.map_sub, ring).
7. (T(D_T) as an integral.) By hT at D_T, and by step 3 together with congrArg (ξ x) and integral_congr_ae, T(D_T) = ∫ ξ(x)(D(x)) dμ.
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 4–7, ∫ g ξ(dη̂) dμ − ∫ g ξ'(η̂) dμ' = T(ω_g) − T(dη_g) = −T(D_T) = −∫ ξ(x)(D(x)) dμ, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: gη and g dη are test forms in U: C^∞, with tsupport inside the compact tsupport η ⊆ U.
Leibniz rule: d(gη)(x) = g(x)dη(x) + alternatizeUncurryFin(Dg(x).smulRight η(x)), by the product rule and linearity of alternatizeUncurryFin.
The representations give ∫gξ(dη)dμ = T(g dη) and ∫gξ'(η)dμ' = ∂T(gη) = T(d(gη)).
Linearity of T and the Leibniz rule give T(g dη) − T(d(gη)) = −T(dg∧η) = −∫ξ(dg∧η)dμ.

subproblems.title: The action integrand of an integer multiplicity triple is integrable
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U (IMRep U n). In particular: M = R.carrier is a Borel set with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable; ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult); ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, operator norm) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M; and for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q (field orients). Here Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then the function x ↦ θ(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = (R.mult x : ℝ) · R.orient x (ω x) is integrable with respect to Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier.

The bound ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1, accepted there as Submission.imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one, is proved inline in step 2.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1, formula (‡) (chapter-06.txt lines 733–746), and step 0(c)–(d) of the parent proof. The integrand of (‡) is integrable because |⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ sup‖ω‖ Hⁿ-a.e. and θ is locally Hⁿ-integrable.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, f := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), K_ω := tsupport f, and G(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(f(x)). Λⁿ and Λ_n = (Λⁿ)* carry operator norms, so |L(α)| ≤ ‖L‖·‖α‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).

1. (The test form.) f is C^∞, hence continuous. K_ω is compact and K_ω ⊆ U, because ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. A continuous function with compact support is bounded, so there is C with ‖f(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Moreover f(x) = 0 for x ∉ K_ω (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), and K_ω is closed, hence Borel.
2. (Orientation bound.) By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for every n-covector α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for every α. Fix such an x and an α. Then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousMultilinearMap.le_opNorm, ‖τ_i‖ = 1), so |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ 1·‖α‖. Hence ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). So ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x.
3. (Dominating function.) Let h := 1_{K_ω}·θ. The map x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable (field measurable_mult, followed by the cast). h is μ-integrable iff θ is integrable for μ⌞K_ω = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K_ω) (integrable_indicator_iff, Measure.restrict_restrict). Since θ ≥ 0 is measurable, this holds when ∫⁻_{M∩K_ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast). That bound is the field locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K_ω ⊆ U. So h and C·h are μ-integrable.
4. (Measurability.) θ is measurable, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and f is continuous. Evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). Hence x ↦ ξ(x)(f(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk, Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable), and so is G.
5. (Domination.) Let x lie in the full-measure set of step 2.
   - If x ∈ K_ω, then |G(x)| ≤ θ(x)·‖ξ(x)‖·‖f(x)‖ ≤ C·θ(x) = C·h(x).
   - If x ∉ K_ω, then f(x) = 0, so G(x) = 0 = C·h(x).
   Hence |G| ≤ C·h μ-a.e.
6. (Conclusion.) By Integrable.mono', G is μ-integrable. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω is continuous with compact support K_ω ⊆ U, so ‖ω‖ ≤ C and ω = 0 off K_ω.
‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x, since |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ for orthonormal τ.
1_{K_ω}θ is integrable by locallyIntegrable_mult, and θξ(ω) is a.e. strongly measurable.
|θξ(ω)| ≤ C·1_{K_ω}θ a.e., so Integrable.mono' gives integrability.

subproblems.title: Dominated convergence for the action of an integer multiplicity triple under bounded pointwise-convergent multipliers
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U of dimension n (IMRep U n, with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient), and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n). Let h_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) be Borel measurable, let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be any function, and let C ∈ ℝ be such that |h_k(x)| ≤ C for all k and x and h_k(x) → h(x) as k → ∞ for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then, with Hⁿ = μHE[n] and Bochner integrals, ∫_M θ(x)·h_k(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) → ∫_M θ(x)·h(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) as k → ∞, where ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = R.orient x (ω x).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the two outer terms of identity (i) converge by dominated convergence), stated once for an arbitrary integer multiplicity triple and test form so that it applies both to (RB, ω) and to (RT, dω). Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier; G(x) := θ(x)·⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (ω x), where ω also denotes the underlying form (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n).

1. (Integrable kernel.) By the sibling action_integrable (Lean `Submission.rsd_cmr_ic_action_integrable P n U R ω`), G is μ-integrable.
2. (Rewriting the integrands.) For every x, θ(x)·h_k(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = h_k(x)·G(x) and θ(x)·h(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = h(x)·G(x), by commutativity and associativity of multiplication in ℝ (`funext` and `ring`). So it suffices to prove ∫ h_k·G dμ → ∫ h·G dμ.
3. (Measurability.) h_k is measurable and real-valued, hence a.e. strongly measurable (`Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable`); G is integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. So F_k := h_k·G is a.e. strongly measurable for μ (`AEStronglyMeasurable.mul`).
4. (Domination.) For every k and x, ‖F_k(x)‖ = |h_k(x)|·‖G(x)‖ ≤ C·‖G(x)‖ (`norm_mul`, the hypothesis |h_k(x)| ≤ C and ‖G(x)‖ ≥ 0, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`). The bound x ↦ C·‖G(x)‖ is μ-integrable (`Integrable.norm`, `Integrable.const_mul`).
5. (Pointwise convergence.) For every x, h_k(x)·G(x) → h(x)·G(x) as k → ∞ (`Tendsto.mul_const` applied to the hypothesis h_k(x) → h(x)).
6. (Dominated convergence.) By steps 3–5 and `tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`, ∫ h_k·G dμ → ∫ h·G dμ. By step 2 this is the claim ∫_M θ·h_k·⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_M θ·h·⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. ∎

subproblems.title: The orientation of an integer multiplicity triple orients the chosen approximate tangent plane a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Then for H^n-almost every x ∈ M (with respect to μHE[n] restricted to M), ξ(x) is a unit orientation of approxTangentPlane n M x. That is, there are orthonormal τ_1, …, τ_n spanning approxTangentPlane n M x such that either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–747): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = τ_1∧⋯∧τ_n with τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) (chapter-03.txt line 86): the approximate tangent space is unique if it exists (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean:232). Write M := R.carrier, ξ := R.orient and μ := μHE[n] restricted to M.

1. By the field R.orients, for μ-almost every x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Fix such x and Q. It suffices to prove approxTangentPlane n M x = Q, because IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) (approxTangentPlane n M x) is then the second property of Q.
2. By definition, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen witness Q₀ of the proposition ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' when this proposition holds, and ⊥ otherwise. Here the proposition holds, with Q as a witness. So approxTangentPlane n M x = Q₀, and by the defining property of the choice, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₀.
3. Approximate tangent planes are unique: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₀ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q imply Q₀ = Q (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Hence approxTangentPlane n M x = Q.
4. Therefore IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) (approxTangentPlane n M x) holds at every x of the full-measure set from step 1, i.e. for μ-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.orients gives, μHE[n]⌞M-a.e., a plane Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q that ξ(x) orients.
At such x, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen witness, which equals Q by HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique.

subproblems.title: A unit orientation of a subspace has operator norm at most 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P (Euclid P), and let ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, i.e. a continuous linear functional on the normed space Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P (operator norms throughout). If ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P spanning Q such that ξ(α) = α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α), then ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.unit_orientation_norm_le_one of DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_measure_unique-a1.orientation_norm_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 0325970d8b47298803106a41abbcdb3c8c9ac103). It is reused here with a byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new worker is provisioned. The argument below is that node's accepted proof; this is step 0(b) of the parent proof.

Source: step 1(c) of the proof of representation independence of θHⁿ⌞M (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3)): for an orthonormal family τ and any n-covector α, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖, so every unit orientation of an n-plane has norm at most 1. Norms: Covector (Euclid P) n is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms with the operator norm, and MultiVector P n is its continuous dual with the operator norm.

1. By the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P (spanning Q; the spanning property is not used below) such that either ξ(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α.
2. Fix an n-covector α. Since α is a continuous multilinear map, |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i=1}^n ‖τ_i‖ (operator-norm bound, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1 (for n = 0 it is the empty product 1). Hence |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. In either sign case of step 1, |ξ(α)| = |±α(τ)| = |α(τ)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
4. Step 3 holds for every n-covector α, and 1 ≥ 0. By the defining property of the operator norm of the continuous linear functional ξ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound), ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. ∎

```lean
  rintro P n Q ξ ⟨τ, hτ, -, hξ⟩
  refine ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ zero_le_one fun α => ?_
  -- `|α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏ᵢ ‖τᵢ‖ = ‖α‖`, as `‖τᵢ‖ = 1`
  have hbound : ‖α τ‖ ≤ ‖α‖ := by
    simpa [hτ.1] using α.le_opNorm τ
  rcases hξ with h | h
  · rw [h, one_mul]
    exact hbound
  · rw [h, norm_neg, one_mul]
    exact hbound
```
